name: Cycle plan
oneLine: 4 coins bought monthly until {date:lastBuy}, held, then sold in thirds from {date:sellWindow.opens} to {date:sellWindow.closes}. The plan rests on a forecast that may not come true.
riskLabel: Very high risk · time-bound bet on a cycle
explanation:
This template encodes a forecast about 2029 that may not come true: that Bitcoin’s highs keep coming about 4 years apart, the next between {date:references.peakFrom} and {date:references.peakTo}. It splits each monthly amount 40 % Bitcoin, 30 % Ethereum, 15 % Solana, and 15 % Chainlink. The plan’s last buy is on {date:lastBuy}, after the halving it places on {date:references.halving}. The plan marks thirds to sell from {date:sellWindow.opens}, from {date:references.secondThird}, and from {date:references.lastThird}, whatever the price. Nothing is held after {date:sellWindow.exitBy}.

People pick it to decide the selling in advance rather than on a day the market moves. What can go wrong: past cycles are too few data points to be a law. The high can come before the window, after it, or not at all. Solana fell 97 % from its high on {date:drawdowns.SOL.high} to its low on {date:drawdowns.SOL.low}. Chainlink fell 91 % from its high on {date:drawdowns.LINK.high} to its low on {date:drawdowns.LINK.low}.

Its dates no longer fill in from {date:validUntil}, and the app then asks for new ones.
